voiceover: Entry five. The guest list has a stranger on it. Norah's Notebook, entry five. The story is fiction. The fix is real. Last time: a reply for six, settled with one kind call. Dear notebook: five weeks out. And a name nobody invited. Mara and I took the printed list for a walk. Halfway down the path, Mara stopped. Who is Rosalind Vance? Not Mara's friend. Not Eli's. Not anyone's, it seemed. Then she found Priya, listed twice, with two spellings. Here's the part people skip. A list doesn't stay clean by itself. Pass one: sort by last name. Duplicates land side by side. Pass two: read every name aloud, as it will be on the envelope. Typos and nicknames jump out when you hear them. Pass three: beside any name you can't place, note who asked for it. Rosalind Vance came from his mother's tab. The note said: we went to her wedding. Do you owe someone an invitation because you went to theirs? No. Zola says you aren't obligated. If your winter wedding list has strangers too, follow along. Entry six is tomorrow. Relatives get a number of names, not a veto. This is the step people skip. Run unsure names through the two questions from entry one. Eli's mother chose her ten. Rosalind made the ranked B list. Wedillybird shows the whole guest list, with each guest's status. Export it to CSV, then sort it any way you like. Sorted. Read aloud. Every name owned. By sunset: one hundred and eight names, every one chosen. I'm Norah, an AI character, and this is Wedillybird. The pen crosses out the stranger, and writes the next problem. The caterer needs the final number by Friday.

caption:
How to cut your wedding guest list: audit it first, then decide every name you can't place.
Entry 05 of Norah's Notebook: three audit passes, the you-went-to-their-wedding myth, and a number (not a veto) for relatives.
Fiction: Norah and the couple are invented. The tips are real.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment: The three audit passes: 1) Sort by last name so duplicates land side by side. 2) Read every name aloud, as it will be written on the envelope. 3) Beside any name you can't place, note who asked for it. Then: you aren't obligated to invite someone just because you went to their wedding, and relatives get a number of names, not a veto (Zola, 2025). Rank your B list so you know who is next (Philadelphia Magazine, 2015). Fiction: Mara, Eli, Rosalind and Norah are invented; the tips are real. Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).
comment_bait: What's the oddest thing you've found on your guest list?

sources.fact: Two-question test for a borderline name: would not inviting them hurt the friendship, and do you care? If yes, B-list; if no, leave them off (callback to entry 01)

claims_review.notes: The audit passes (sort, read aloud, note who asked) are Norah's practical suggestions, not statistics. Story numbers (five weeks, one hundred and eight names, ten names for a relative) and the names Rosalind Vance and Priya are invented. The product is shown only as S07 (list with statuses, then CSV export), about seven seconds, in the brand's voice, with no claim that it detects duplicates or typos. The two-question test and the B-list ranking are callbacks to entry 01, kept to one beat each so the entry does not duplicate the later Copy, Paste, Send episode on parents.
